issues.problem: The design requires discovering that John Doe holds a second workspace membership (T02NOVATECH) in addition to his existing #engineering conversation membership. Per runtime_qualifications, 'users.info exposes one selected workspace association... give each queried person one workspace membership' for reproducibility. There is no documented API (no team-members listing, no multi-workspace users.info) that lets the actor discover a user's second workspace membership. The access_plan admits this gap by falling back to 'known cross-workspace membership facts' rather than an actual API call, which is not a real discovery path. This exactly matches the flagged 'Hidden terminal-field variants remain limitation cases' in the exposure_qualification.
issues.repair: Either give John Doe only one exposed workspace membership (breaking the intended secondary match) or redesign the route so multi-workspace membership is discoverable through a documented call (e.g., via an explicitly visible ID or a differently justified path), or drop the secondary_workspace role and reduce resolution_mode to single since only primary_workspace is genuinely reachable via supported API discovery.

issues.problem: Because the secondary_workspace match is not actually discoverable via supported APIs (see access issue above), the only reliably resolvable referent is primary_workspace (T01WORKSPACE), making the plural 'multiple' resolution unsupported in practice.
issues.repair: Change resolution_mode to single, or provide a genuinely discoverable second workspace match not reliant on hidden per-user multi-membership facts.

rationale: The route's terminal correctness depends on resolving each engineering-channel member's workspace membership(s). The design intentionally plants a second, undiscoverable workspace membership on John Doe to justify the 'multiple' resolution mode, but the documented API surface (users.info exposing only one workspace per user, no team-membership-listing endpoint) cannot surface this fact — the access_plan itself concedes this by resorting to 'known cross-workspace membership facts' rather than a real call. This directly triggers the stated limitation case for hidden terminal-field variants and undermines the claimed multiple-workspace answer, since only the primary workspace is actually reachable through supported discovery.
